page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.large is an entry-level virtual server instance within the compute-optimized family, running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8163 processor clocked at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core using hyper-threading, accompanied by 2.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Architectural CPU feature flags include support for AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX512 VNNI), AES, BMI2, and FMA instructions.

Hardware configurations exclude integrated local instance storage and dedicated hardware accelerators, necessitating the attachment of network-attached block storage for operating system and data requirements. Baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provided with the base deployment.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily within the lower percentiles across compute and memory workloads. The single-core stress-ng metric reached 1098.29, while multi-core throughput registered at 1457.69. PassMark testing yielded a CPU mark of 1820.93 and a memory score of 881.34. Memory throughput tests show large-block read operations at 10.26 GB/sec and write operations at 9.37 GB/sec. Application testing reflected 1.43 million operations per second in Redis SET commands and 1.77 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

Given its minimal 2.0 GB memory capacity and dual-thread execution envelope, the instance presents qualitative cost efficiency for resource-light applications requiring predictable dedicated CPU cycles rather than shared-core scheduling. Primary workload fits include lightweight utility scripts, basic microservices, small internal monitoring agents, low-concurrency network tasks, and lightweight API routing where memory footprints remain minimal.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.large is a compute-oriented virtual server configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 2.0 GB of RAM on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Operating via the KVM hypervisor, it features a 1-core, 2-thread execution layout equipped with AVX-512 instruction extensions. The instance includes no local storage or onboard GPUs, relying on remote network volumes and offering a baseline network capacity of 1 Gbps. In standardized performance evaluations, the system registers lower-tier outputs, scoring 1820.93 on PassMark CPU tests and delivering 10.26 GB/sec on uncached memory reads. The strict 1:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio restricts large in-memory frameworks but serves lightweight dedicated tasks effectively. The instance fits small web proxies, background automation workers, monitoring agents, and low-traffic microservices.
